context_requirements: Cells must be actively replicating and dependent on ribonucleotide reductase for dNTP supply.
Intact DNA damage checkpoint signaling (ATM/ATR-CHK1/CHK2-p53) is needed for the transcriptional response.
p53 status modulates the strength of CDKN1A and pro-apoptotic gene induction.
High RRM2 expression or oncogene-driven replication stress may increase sensitivity.
falsifiers: No induction of CDKN1A, GADD45A, or RRM2 at 6 h in any cell line.
No decrease in S-phase or proliferation-related genes at 24 h.
No difference in response between cell lines with intact versus defective p53.
Lack of any transcriptional response across all nine lines.

evidence.supports: Ribonucleotide reductase is regulated by checkpoint kinases and its inhibition affects DNA replication.
RNR is transcriptionally induced after DNA damage via ATM/CHK2 checkpoint pathways.
Ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor hydroxyurea triggers replicational stress and apoptosis in cancer cells.
Ribonucleotide reductase inhibitor didox affects cell cycle and radiosensitivity in PC-3 prostate cancer cells.
Ribonucleotide reductase inhibition activates CHK1 and induces apoptosis in Ewing sarcoma cells.
